column1: # P4-130 — which upstream libjpeg-turbo release each C oracle runs against.
# Every differential gate in this repository is only as current as the C
# library it compares against. Upstream shipped 3.2.0 on 2026-06-30 and it took
# two months for anyone to notice that all thirteen oracle pins still said
# 3.1.4.1 — because the version lived in thirteen shell fragments across five
# workflow files and nowhere else. This file is the single place that answers
# "which release does a green gate prove parity with?".
# `tests/oracle_version_pins.rs` enforces it in both directions: a workflow pin
# with no row here fails, and a row here that no workflow installs fails.
# `scripts/check_oracle_currency.sh` asks the remaining question — whether
# upstream has moved past `tool-current` — on a weekly schedule.
# Roles:
#   tool-baseline  the release the existing expectations were written against.
#                  Kept as its own leg on purpose: bumping it in place would
#                  re-baseline every expectation at once, and any divergence
#                  that hid behind the bump would be indistinguishable from a
#                  pass.
#   tool-current   current upstream stable, and therefore the parity target.
#   submodule      references/libjpeg-turbo. Not a tool pin: it is built in CI
#                  as the classic-ABI trace oracle (`/tmp/ljt8/prefix`, v8 ABI)
#                  and it is the source every `j*.c:NNN` citation quotes.
# role
tool-baseline
column5: Behaviour-regression leg: djpeg/cjpeg/jpegtran + libturbojpeg for the differential suites, at the release the current expectations were written against.

column1: tool-current
column5: Current-parity leg: the same differential suites against current upstream stable, selected explicitly through LIBJPEG_TURBO_PREFIX rather than PATH order.

column1: submodule
column5: Classic-ABI trace oracle built with WITH_JPEG8=1, and the source tree the C citations quote. Already on the 3.2 line, which is why the tool pins and the citations disagreed unnoticed.
